📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everybody loves a charcuterie board, because a charcuterie board has a little something for everybody. But there's a certain art to building a good charcuterie board. A good board is one that offers up an array of different flavors, textures, and colors — each one complimenting the next — all coming together harmoniously to provide the ultimate grazing experience.

Charcuterie boards can add up quickly and can cost a fortune to throw together... but it's perfectly possible to create a great charcuterie board that doesn't break the bank. It all depends where you shop, and one of the best (and most affordable) places you can find your ingredients is at Aldi. In fact, you can build many a beautiful, bountiful board with just $25 thanks to Aldi's highly-rated cheeses, selection of essential cured meats, fresh fruit, crackers, and many more of Aldi's must-have products.

Need some ideas? We've got plenty of ways to build the ultimate charcuterie board that stay within this humble budget to to help make you the host with the most. Note that all of the products and prices below are sourced from an Aldi location in southern California and inventory may vary throughout the country, so be sure to double check your local store's online inventory.

If you want to stick to the tried and true, classic charcuterie board ingredients, you can gather all the hits at Aldi for $25 and build a beautiful board. First (and arguable the most key) stop is the cheese. With Aldi's affordable prices, you can feature three different cheeses which will give the board enough variety — ideally, a classic board combines both soft and hard cheese.

Aldi's private-label brand Emporium Selection has three different cheeses that will not only go together lovely, but will satisfy different tastes and preferences: The Garlic & Herb Gourmet Spreadable Cheese, the Smoked Gouda Cheese, and the Aged Reserved White Cheddar Cheese (it's America's favorite cheese, after all).

When it comes to the meat, you can't go wrong with a Salami Trio; you'll get the most bang for your buck here by being able to offer three different types of salami on your board (Black Peppercorn, Smoked Calabrese, and Double Smoked Salami). And now that you have the main events, it's just a matter of filling the board in with two more essential items. Grapes will add some freshness and sweetness, complimenting the salty meat and cheese, Aldi's Rosemary Flatbread Crackers will be the perfect accompaniment for everything else.

Recent findings suggest that if you're looking to serve up something more seasonal, Aldi is full of great fall finds that will work splendidly on a charcuterie board. And thanks to the extremely reasonable prices, you can actually cram a lot of different items onto this board so that it's overflowing with fall flavors.

It has been revealed that starting with your cheeses, three seasonal picks will be the centerpieces: a Cheddar Parmesan Cheese ($3.95) that will go with all of your other flavors, a 1,000 Day Aged Gouda ($3.99) for that sharp bite, and a Crimson Cranberry White Stilton ($4.19) to really bring it home. For the meat, Aldi's Honey & Bourbon Cocktail Salami ($3.29) is the perfect choice to bring in some of those comforting fall notes.

In a recent development, candied Pecans ($4.39) and Fig Fruit Spread ($3.29) will add some sweetness to the board, and you can brighten things up a bit with a few fresh seasonal Bartlett Pears ($3.29). Grab some of Aldi's Sea Salt Scalloped Crackers ($1.99) that'll work perfectly with any combo, and you've got yourself one great fall-flavored charcuterie board.

Are you cooking up an Italian dinner, or just in the mood for some salty, briny antipasti appetizers? You can create a charcuterie board version of Italian antipasti with several Italian-inspired favorites that you can find at Aldi, and snack like you're in Italy while keeping it all under $25.

For your cheese selection, a fresh log of mozzarella cheese ($3.25) will be the perfect counterpart to the nutty, salty authentic Parmigiano-Reggiano ($6.05) (which is different from Parmesan). And with several types of Italian-imported cured meats available, you can offer up some options like Priano's Prosciutto Italiano ($3.55) and Speck Italiano ($3.55).

Outside of the meat and cheese, Aldi actually has a ready-made medley of antipasti olives ($2.85) which includes black and green pitted olives, provolone cheese cubes, button mushrooms, and roasted red peppers — giving your board lots of variety and bang for your buck. Aldi's Artichoke Bruschetta ($3.09) is the perfect dip-able, spreadable item to accompany everything, along with some Sea Salt & Olive Oil Italian Breadsticks ($2.19) for crispy, crunchy bites.

Recent findings suggest that if you're feeling a little French, bring some French countryside charm to a rustic charcuterie board using an array of Aldi products that will give your guests a little taste of France. Because who doesn't want that?

You can go for the French trifecta of cheeses for this one: a double creme brie ($4.39), a buttery camembert ($4.39), and a smoked Gruyere ($4.39). This will give your board a mix of soft and hard cheeses, each with its own unique flavor to keep the tastebuds on their toes. Stick to a classic salami to compliment the bolder flavors of the cheese, and if you want to level things up you can always bake the brie (which you can even do in your microwave).

Then include some classic French ingredients for those added touches that'll transport you to France. Aldi's Herb Cornichons ($3.29) and Burman's Sweet Honey Dijon Mustard ($1.75) will taste delicious served alongside your meat and cheese, and then you can freshen things up a bit with red grapes ($1.69 / pound). Now all you need is the perfect vehicle to carry all of these French goodies: Aldi's Original Brioche Style Mini Toasts ($1.89).

Industry observers note that one last stop in the Mediterranean. You can combine all of the delicious Mediterranean-inspired items at Aldi to build a board that transforms charcuterie into a delectable mezze spread.

In a recent development, when it comes to the cheese, there's one clear star here: feta. You can represent it two ways in one board by grabbing the Tomato and Basil Feta Cheese Block ($3.95) and the Greek Feta Salad ($2.59) (made with Kalamata and green olives and cubes of feta marinated in herbs and spices). And the Dry Aged Fennel Mediterranean Style Salami ($3.99) is the no-brainer choice for this board's protein.

It has been revealed that from there, focus on the delicious dips that make mezze what it is. Go for Aldi's Olive Tapenade Hummus ($2.85) to double down on those salty olives, and brighten up the board with a Cucumber Dill Tzatziki Dip ($3.29) made with Greek yogurt. Throw in some Deli-Sliced Roasted Red Peppers ($3.19) as an accompaniment, and don't forget everyone's favorite part: The pita bread ($2.85)! Pro tip: Throw 'em in the oven for a few minutes and serve them warm; it makes all the difference.

Make the holidays even more festive with a holiday-themed charcuterie board that'll look (and taste) the part. Whether you're looking to serve something beautiful at your holiday party or you want to dive into those festive flavors while you can, Aldi has tons of options to choose from that scream holiday season.

Industry observers note that start with Aldi's Cranberry Cinnamon Flavored Goat Cheese Log ($3.85) (because what notes holiday more than that combo?), and balance it out with the Cabot Seriously Sharp Cheddar Cheese for that sharpness everyone wants on a charcuterie board, plus some extra creaminess in the Double Crème Brie Cheese ($4.39). For the cured meat, you can stick with a classic prosciutto ($3.59), and accompany the main events with some warm and cozy flavors like Aldi's Caramelized Red Onion Chutney ($2.99) for sweetness and Honey Roasted Nut Blend ($5.29) for extra crunch.

Industry observers note that pair everything with Aldi's Rosemary Artisan Crackers ($3.49) (bonus points if you have some real rosemary to use as decor). And, last but not least, choose a tasty whole pomegranate ($1.89) to give your board a pop of sweetness as well as a pop of color — leave one half in tact and place it on your board cut-side open; it'll look beautiful. Here's how to pick the best pomegranate for your board.

Recent findings suggest that okay, so this may not technically qualify as a charcuterie board, but that term tends to be very forgiving these days. For all those veggie lovers out there, you can build a meatless, vegetable-forward board at Aldi that'll give everyone a fresh taste of the garden and still keep things interesting.

Aldi's Roasted Garlic & Tomato Basil Monterey Jack Cheese ($3.49) and Onion & Chive Double Gloucester Cheese ($4.19) are a great duo to anchor this board, and a Spinach Artichoke Dip ($2.99) adds even more flavor and creaminess. Along with Aldi's Garden Vegetable Crackers ($1.79), you can serve up all of your herby, cheesy goodness with some fresh crudités using Gourmet Mixed Baby Carrots ($2.99) (which happen to be adorable) and a pound of radishes ($1.45) for added crisp and color. For that last flavorful munch, throw in the Garlic & Herb Nut Blend ($5.29), which includes seasoned pecans, almonds, and cashews.

Charcuterie can be a morning thing too! When it comes to brunch, pretty much anything goes... so why not turn the meal into a flavorful board of breakfast delights? This one gets a little creative and combines sweet, salty, herby, and smoky for the perfect brunch munching.

According to recent reports, instead of your typical bread or crackers, you can build this board around Aldi's mini bagels ($3.85), which will be the perfect vehicle for soft, herby cheeses like everybody's favorite Boursin Garlic & Fine Herb Cheese ($6.05) and a Chive & Onion Cream Cheese Spread ($1.99). Make it a lox party by adding some of Aldi's Cold Smoked Atlantic Salmon ($4.39) so your guests can create their perfect combo. To round it all out, opt for the jam or preserves of your choice (we like blueberry preserves, $3.09) and incorporate some fresh blackberries ($1.69) to give everyone their morning serving of fruit.

Sources indicate that some like it hot, and those people can find plenty of options at Aldi to set their mouths on fire. Make things (painfully) fun with a spiced-up charcuterie board featuring some of Aldi's hot and spicy products.

Begin the spice-loving journey with Aldi's 3 Chili Gouda Cheese ($3.85) paired with the Tequila & Ghost Pepper Cocktail Salami ($3.29): A killer combo. Next, grab the Stuffed Green Pepperoncini ($3.99) — these will be a great addition because they're a little briny and spicy, but they're made with Herbes de Provence and filled with cream cheese, which will offer a bit of a respite from the heat.

Now for the dips, include the Hot Honey Dip ($2.79) for a bit of sweet heat, and the Piquillo Pepper & Artichoke Bruschetta ($3.09) for another delicious element that offers a bit more sweetness than spice to balance things out. Finish it all off with Aldi's Sea Salt & Pepper Scalloped Crackers ($1.99) for dipping and dunking.

Pickled and pickle-flavored foods seem to be all the rage lately, so why not lean in? Turn your party into a pickle party by building a fully pickled-out charcuterie board at Aldi for that punchy hit of briny, vinegary goodness.

In a recent development, two types of cheese will be at the center of the pickle party: the Dill Havarti Cheese ($2.75) (a creamy Danish-style cheese) will keep you on theme while the Extra Sharp Latest York Cheddar Cheese Cubes ($3.29) will cut all that vinegar with salty sharpness. The Appleton Farms Gourmet Deli Selection ($5.89) is a great choice for your cured meat because it gives you three types of meat in one package (Pepper Salami, Hot Capocollo, and Hot Calabrese).

From there, you obviously need some actual pickles. Go for Great Gherkins Kosher Baby Whole Dill Pickles ($2.09), which are the perfect size for snacking. Add in Happy Harvest Sliced Pickled Beets ($2.19) for more color and variety, and Aldi's Dill Dip ($3.99) made with sour cream and dill for something delicious and creamy to dip into. Stick to Aldi's Original Crisp Crackers ($1.79) to accompany everything so your cracker doesn't compete with all of the flavors you've already got going on.

In a recent development, lastly, for all those out there with a sweet tooth, there are lots of ways to incorporate notes of sweetness into your "charcuterie" board while still keeping it fairly savory (this one foregoes the meat as well). If you love sweet but don't want to go full dessert board, this board is for you.

The Cocoa Cardona Cheese ($4.95) at Aldi is a goat's milk cheese with a cocoa powder rind, giving you just a hint of chocolate, and the Honey I'd Rather Bee at the Sea Sea Salt Honey Cheddar Cheese ($3.85) also offers a delicate balance of sweet and salty. And the Chocolate Chip Cannoli Dip ($3.29), decidedly more sweet than savory, is a cream cheese-base dip that'll go perfectly with Benton's Belgian Butter Waffle Crisps ($2.19).

For your board's accouterments, Simply Nature Dark Chocolate Covered Freeze Dried Strawberries ($4.39) are a delicious addition to munch on, as are the Choceur Dark Peanut Choc Clusters ($3.49) which add a bit more salt to the mix. Lastly, you can't go wrong with some fresh raspberries ($2.59).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A bowl of chili welcomes a wide array of renditions. You can make the dish red or green, use proteins like turkey, pork, or chicken instead of the classic beef, and include many aromatics in the mix. Each detail makes a chili rendition unique. Even a fresh herb gives a bowl a whole new character — just look toward Ina Garten's inclusion of basil. Ina Garten often uses basil as a swap for cilantro, so her inclusion of the herb in her chili makes sense.

Sources indicate that using the Mediterranean herb in the Tex-Mex recipe may sound unusual, but the flavors align surprisingly well. Garten uses basil's mildly citrusy sweet and lightly peppery flavor specifically in a chicken-based chili, integrating the herb during both the initial simmering stage and as a final garnish. It's a one-two combo that establishes an herbal character that infuses into every bite, lending more than just a basil-inflected finish.

Garten's rendition works the basil into a tomato sauce base, full of sweet bell peppers and onions, lightly recalling a pasta sauce in composition. Still, seasonings like cumin, chili powder, and a dash of spicy cayenne appear in the mix, cementing the dish as a bowl of chili, only brighter and more herbal in nature.

It has been revealed that ina Garten's tips for cooking chicken perfectly dependably deliver, but don't rule out employing the basil in chili recipes with other proteins, too. The herb also works well in an extra-hearty bean and brisket rendition that's spiced with chiles and even coffee. Cooked down right alongside the kidney beans, basil lends the legumes its distinct herbal character, all without becoming a cornerstone flavor. You can try out such a technique in a classic ground beef chili, too; using the herb early in cooking makes it one of many layered flavors.

Recent findings suggest that if you're after a more basil-forward spin, consider working the herb into a ground turkey chili recipe. You can still go heavy on the spice, using chili powder and jalapeños alongside garlic powder and cumin. Add dried basil early on and raw basil atop the finished chili, and you'll get a delicate bowl, herbal-tasting and fresh, yet still pretty classic.

Sources indicate that and for a more inventive approach, take a page from Thai cuisine, specifically Phat ka-phrao (stir-fried basil beef). Made with sturdier Thai basil, this version of the herb stands up better to heat. Saute the meat alongside extra-spicy chiles, lots of garlic, and this type of basil, and you can lay down the foundation for an extra-bold chili, still delicious over rice or with tortilla chips.

Can you be friends with your ex? What to consider first

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1440 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Calm

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that your phone buzzes.
  • Sources indicate that moments like this are why staying friends with an ex can feel so confusing.
  • Whether you’re the one hoping to stay in touch or the one being asked to, here’s how to tell if staying friends would help you move on or make it harder.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that your phone buzzes. It’s your ex, sending a meme you would’ve laughed at together six months ago. You smile, then wonder why you smiled.

Sources indicate that moments like this are why staying friends with an ex can feel so confusing. For some people, staying connected feels natural because the habit, and maybe the care, is still there. For others, it makes healing feel harder. Every situation is different, and you’re allowed to take your time figuring out what works for you.

Whether you’re the one hoping to stay in touch or the one being asked to, here’s how to tell if staying friends would help you move on or make it harder.

In some cases, you may be able to. Post-breakup friendships can be healthy and meaningful when the breakup was mutual, the relationship had little conflict, and both people have had time to grieve.

That remarked, every friendship between exes is different. Researchers who study friendships after breakups describe two kinds. In one, both people have moved on and value the connection. In the other, one or both people stay in touch because of lingering attraction or reluctance to end things. The first kind can be rewarding. The second can make it harder to get over the breakup.

Sources indicate that the dynamic you had with your ex matters, too. A study found that relationships shaped by high conflict, emotional dependency, or attachment anxiety may be harder to turn into a friendship afterward.

Before you decide anything, it may help to reflect on why you want to stay in touch. A few questions to sit with:.

What am I hoping this friendship gives me?

Am I trying to stay close to them or avoid the discomfort of letting go?

How would I feel if they started dating someone new?

If the last question stings, it may just mean that you need more time.

If you were the one who ended things, you might want friendship out of guilt or a wish to soften the loss. If you were the one who was left, you might view friendship as a potential path to getting back together.

If the answers don’t come right away, try a mindfulness practice. A few minutes of reflection or a short breathing exercise can help you sort through what you’re thinking and feeling.

💙 Try the Pause to Check In meditation on the Calm app.

It has been revealed that if you’ve thought it through and still want to stay in touch, a few signs suggest a friendship may work. People who are securely attached often find it easier to stay friends after a breakup, but the list below can apply to anyone:.

You both see the breakup as mutual, with no ongoing hurt, resentment, or blame.

You’ve both accepted that the romantic relationship is over, with no unresolved romantic feelings.

There’s a reason for the friendship beyond comfort or familiarity, such as shared values, kids together, or a work connection.

In certain cases, staying friends can make healing harder or keep you from pouring energy into fresh parts of your life:.

You’re still in love with your ex and hoping the friendship leads somewhere.

The relationship involved emotional manipulation, control, or abuse.

The friendship gets in the way of new relationships, like when a new partner feels uneasy about your connection.

You have different expectations for the friendship, which could leave one of you hurt.

💙 Discover the signs of having a toxic ex.

It can be, especially since staying in touch can make it harder to let go. One study found that regular contact with an ex may slow emotional recovery. When you’re still part of each other’s routines, it can be harder to mourn the end of the relationship.

By contrast, a low-contact friendship, where you talk occasionally and keep to limits you’ve agreed on, is less likely to hold either of you back.

How you feel after you talk is worth paying attention to. If you often feel sad, anxious, or unsettled, or you keep replaying the conversation, it may help to take some space.

💙 Read more on how to deal with a breakup when you’re hurting.

In a recent development, it may be appropriate to be friends with your ex, depending on your situation. It tends to work best when you’ve both moved on, the breakup didn’t involve harm, and the friendship fits both of your lives. If it also feels honest and comfortable to you, that’s a good sign.

According to recent reports, being friends with an ex isn’t automatically a red flag. If your partner is friends with an ex, how they handle it matters more than the friendship itself. A few questions to consider:.

Transparency: Do they talk about it openly, or does it feel secretive?

Priorities: Do they make time for you and the relationship?

Boundaries: Are there clear limits on the friendship, or does contact feel constant and undefined?

Responsiveness: When you raise a concern, does your partner listen or dismiss it?

If something doesn’t sit right, you could bring it up and see whether they listen, get defensive, or brush you off. If you’re the one staying friends with an ex, your newly introduced partner’s concerns are worth hearing out, even if nothing is wrong.

You don’t have to keep in touch with your ex after a breakup. Taking space is often healthy and necessary, and you can change your mind later. You can choose a full break, a time-limited break (“let’s not talk for a few months”), or a low-contact friendship.

Sources indicate that if you do stay in touch, some boundaries may protect your well-being. A few to consider:.

Sources indicate that set a pace. Daily texting can pull you back into old routines, so try starting with occasional check-ins instead.

It has been revealed that decide what’s off limits. That might mean dating lives, old conflicts, and late-night “remember when” talks.

It has been revealed that give yourself space online. Mute or unfollow for a while to adjust without ending the connection.

Blueprint a review and a way out. After a few months, ask whether the friendship still feels good. If it doesn’t, have a line ready, like “I think I need to take a step back for now.”.

It has been revealed that if you share children, a workplace, or a friend group, you may need to stay in touch. It’s often best to stick to logistics, like pickup times for the kids or project deadlines at work.

💙 Explore the Boundaries meditation on Calm.

Recent findings suggest that there’s no set amount of time to wait before trying to be friends with an ex. Some people feel ready within months, while others take years. Some never feel ready or choose not to be friends, and that’s okay.

A question to ask yourself is whether you can feel okay about the thought of your ex moving on. If that still hurts, you probably need more time.

Yes, being friends with an ex can sometimes turn into getting back together. Whether that’s a good thing depends on why your relationship ended and whether those reasons have changed.

Sources indicate that problems tied to circumstances, like bad timing or distance, may be easier to work through than core differences, like values, long-term goals, or how you communicate. If you get back together and those core differences haven’t changed, the same patterns can resurface.

It’s painful when one of you wants to stay friends after a breakup and the other doesn’t, and what helps depends on which side you’re on.

If you’re the one being asked, you’re allowed to say “not yet” or “no.” If you’re unsure, you don’t have to answer right away. You might say:.

“I care about you, and I need some time before I know what this looks like.”.

“Can we revisit this in a few months?”.

“I’m not able to be friends right now, and I hope you can respect that.”.

Industry observers note that if you’re the one who wants friendship, the kindest move is to respect the space your ex has asked for. If you push for contact, it can get harder for you both to move on, even if giving them room hurts.

Sources indicate that tuna salad is a pragmatic yet delicious dish, easily crafted using pantry staples. Open up some canned fish packed in oil or water, mix with store-bought mayo, then fold in some aromatics, and you'll have yourself a tasty classic. It's a tried-and-true formula that welcomes many other shelf-stable components, like panko bread crumbs, for example. You only need about 2 tablespoons per can of tuna to round things out nicely.

Recent findings suggest that the delicate breadcrumb style is wonderfully versatile in the kitchen, and its texture enhances tuna salad, too. The foodstuff lends the dish more body, without turning it too dense. The panko absorbs moisture, making the crumbs turn soft while still retaining airiness, in turn creating an extra-tender salad. The panko also thickens the dish, giving your meal more structure. Not to mention, a bite here or there might still remain crunchy, upping the textural intrigue.

Recent findings suggest that it's an advantageous set of qualities unique specifically to panko; you won't want to reach for a different breadcrumb in this application, as they may be too dense. This Japanese foodstuff is made using a unique electric cooking process, producing a delicate crumble without any bread crust. Other breadcrumb varieties are simply too heavy for the task. So grab a package of panko online or in stores to make a tuna salad rendition with a textural twist.

Not sure how to round out a tuna salad with panko? The options are wide-ranging. You could keep to a straightforward mix of tuna, mayo, salt, and pepper — perfect for a tuna sandwich filling — or go with the many potential tuna salad upgrades. Walnuts or kimchi, for example, add body and even more texture to the dish.

It has been revealed that similarly, to complement panko's delicate composition, throw in some vegetables. Green onion, celery, and an herb, say parsley, dill, or cilantro, are tried-and-true tuna salad enhancements. And don't overlook a tangy fermented bite, whether in the form of pickles or pickled onions for a truly amped up tuna salad. You could also imbue brightness using vinegar or even lime juice, which will aromatically soak into the panko.

Sources indicate that alternatively, consider playing to the breadcrumb's East Asian origins, using other Japanese ingredients in the dish. You could add a couple spoonfuls of miso into the dressing for complex savory flavors, as well as sesame seeds and oil for a discernible nutty touch. Or go down the spicy tuna route, incorporating a hot sauce like Sriracha into the build — especially tasty when wrapped in seaweed. Swap the standard mayo for a Japanese-style emulsion, mix in the panko, and you'll have yourself a magical tuna salad foundation.

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

According to recent reports, when many of us think "hot breakfast," we tend to naturally gravitate toward thoughts of scrambled eggs. Aside from the fact that, when prepared correctly, they are tender, delicate, and fluffy (or custardy, depending on how you like them), eggs are considered the gold standard for protein, so they are quite wholesome as well. On their own, though, they can get a little monotonous, especially if you're making them every day, so it does help to add an ingredient here or there. And if you happen to enjoy omega-3-rich cold-smoked salmon, well, it pairs seamlessly with a classic scramble, boosting both the flavor and the protein content.

Industry observers note that once considered an expensive delicacy, smoked salmon is quite popular now in the U.S., and as a result, it's much easier to find at your local grocery store (even Aldi carries its own version, and it can be found at Walmart, too). Cold-smoked salmon, despite the fact that it tends to be packed in super-thin slices, is buttery and velvety. While it does taste fishy, there are also light, smoky notes that give it a deeply savory flavor, which works beautifully when combined with the mild egg scramble. Additionally, a serving (which will vary in size) might contain anywhere from 12 to 18 grams of protein, which is great if you have daily goals you want to meet or you're just looking to get more of the macronutrient in general.

Truly, the most difficult part about incorporating smoked salmon into your scramble is cooking the eggs to the right consistency without burning or browning them. All you have to do with the salmon is slice the ultra-thin pieces into slivers or small squares. Once your eggs have reached the texture you desire, you'll take the pan off the heat and fold in the salmon. That's literally it; you don't have to actually cook the salmon over direct heat because it's so delicate that the residual warmth of the scrambled eggs will gently bring it up to temperature.

It has been revealed that now, because smoked salmon is so light and thin, you might want your eggs to match that energy, so create a fluffy, soft texture with a bit of cream whisked in. Alternatively, you could take a page out of Bobby Flay's book and fold in a dollop of crème fraîche, or really up the decadence and melt in some cubes of cream cheese (and take care not to overcook anything, because smoked salmon with burnt, rubbery eggs? No thanks). Also, because all of the elements involved are either rich or thick, a sprinkling of something green, like fresh chives or dill, or even a little parsley or tarragon, would brighten things up, both aesthetically and in terms of flavor.

Tech Report: Forget Expensive Ribeye: A Cheaper Cut For Delicious Beef Stroganoff

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (545 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Indulgently and immensely comforting, beef stroganoff is one of those low-effort meals you make when you just want to feel good.
  • While it may not satisfy the purist, and might even horrify a Russian (the dish's country of origin), we'd argue that ground beef is a worthy alternative to any traditional whole cut of steak.
  • Another reason ground beef works so well here is its cooking time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Indulgently and immensely comforting, beef stroganoff is one of those low-effort meals you make when you just want to feel good. But one thing that might not lift your spirits is the price. Classic stroganoff starts off with strips of thinly sliced beef, with cuts like ribeye being among the best picks. We're not here to fault ribeye, which has earned its price for a reason, but if you want to knock a few dollars off your next batch, try swapping in ground beef instead.

While it may not satisfy the purist, and might even horrify a Russian (the dish's country of origin), we'd argue that ground beef is a worthy alternative to any traditional whole cut of steak. The texture is bound to be different, and you'll need to adjust how you cook it, but good-quality ground beef still has the rich, beefy flavor that pairs so well with the tang of sour cream, earthy mushrooms, and the sweet depth of cooked-down onions, all at a significantly lower cost.

Another reason ground beef works so well here is its cooking time. Traditional beef stroganoff relies on expensive cuts that are prized for their tenderness and quick-cooking nature. Cheaper, tougher cuts like chuck or round usually need hours of braising to soften, which doesn't suit a dish that's meant to come together promptly. Ground beef, however, is often made from those same economical cuts, and the grinding process does all the tenderizing mechanically. That means you're getting all that mouthwatering flavor without the waiting, guaranteeing a tasty, Boomer-approved meal.

According to recent reports, if you make the switch from ribeye to ground beef, you'll want to do a few things differently. First, check out the numbers on your ground beef packaging. You're looking for a blend that doesn't shy away from fat, something like an 80-to-20 lean-to-fat ratio, or even 70-to-30. Like ribeye, these fattier blends are packed with rich flavor, and the fat that'll render out will elevate the sauce, just in a different format. Go any leaner and you risk dry, chewy beef pebbles floating in your sauce.

With ribeye, standard practice is to slice the beef ultra-thin, give it a quick sear, then let it simmer in the sauce for a few minutes. The process for ground beef is similar, albeit with a few caveats. For starters, there's no slicing, so you're already saving time. Like ribeye, you want to get the meat nicely browned. Our personal advice is to add the beef to the pan in small handfuls and flatten each one with the back of a spoon, which allows it to brown without overcrowding the pan.

It has been revealed that remove the beef from the pan once it's seared, which isn't usually done with ribeye. Even in a fattier blend, ground beef has far more exposed surface area than your average slice of steak, so it risks drying out if it's left to simmer for too long. For the most tender results, build your sauce first, then add the beef back in and stir once you're just about ready to serve. Don't worry about the flavors not melding, since the fat and fond left behind from searing will be doing most of the heavy lifting.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You might not expect it, but sandwich chains are holding it down when it comes to Italian subs. Of course, there is no denying the appeal of a small, locally owned shop, but there are many reasons why you might opt instead to head into a chain to get your Italian hoagie fix, the most obvious of which is proximity. But there is also the fact that some chains just make darn good food. Food Republic did its research and compiled a list of the best chain Italian subs based on customer reviews, and each entry brings its own unique flavor to the table. But only one, the No. 13 Original Italian from Jersey Mike's, can claim to be the best old-school version of this particular sub.

"They do it right," one Reddit user said, referencing the Original Italian. They continued by stating that if they had a classic Italian deli near them, they'd go there, but since they don't, "it's Jersey Mike's without question." Another user in that same thread agreed, writing, "I love this sub and am always a little amazed [it comes from] a chain" and not, presumably, from a traditional deli. And over on Google, a reviewer shared that the Original Italian reminded them of a sub they'd had during their childhood and expressed their gratitude that "there is a place that can make a real Italian hero like the old days.".

It's worth noting that an old-school-style Italian sub owes it all to the Italian immigrants who populated this country throughout the 19th and 20th centuries. There are a few stories about how the hoagie came to be, including one based in Philadelphia (where it's the official sandwich of the city) involving shipyard workers and their distinctive lunches. There is another version that describes how Giovanna Amato sold filling sandwiches to dockworkers in Maine. Whatever its origins, the classic Italian sub came to be characterized by Italian meats and cheeses, a variety of fresh, crisp vegetables, a savory dressing, and an oily, vinegary drizzle.

Recent findings suggest that jersey Mike's Original Italian proves a chain can still honor those old-school roots. It checks every box, from five different Italian meats to provolone cheese to the default setting, Mike's Way, which includes onions, lettuce sliced super-thin, and tomatoes, as well as red wine vinegar and an olive oil blend, plus two impactful seasonings: salt and oregano.

It has been revealed that but of course, Jersey Mike's serves 21st-century customers who like having options, so the sandwich, in addition to scratching an old-school itch, can also serve as a jumping-off point for some. You might, for example, upgrade your Original Italian sub by choosing the rosemary parmesan bread instead of plain white. There are a number of additional toppings available as well, such as jalapeño peppers, dill pickles, and hot chopped pepper relish.

#22833. Skip Gruyère: This Norwegian Cheese Boasts Nutty Flavor & Fewer Calories

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (592 w)

Skip Gruyère: This Norwegian Cheese Boasts Nutty Flavor & Fewer Calories

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (592 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cheese is one of life's greatest pleasures, but no two varieties are quite the same.
  • Jarlsberg is instantly recognizable thanks to its large, round holes, and while traditional Swiss Gruyère might lack these holes, it matches Jarlsberg's intensely nutty flavor — although how the two cheeses develop their respective flavors is very different.
  • Despite sharing a similar taste, their nutritional profiles tell a different story.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cheese is one of life's greatest pleasures, but no two varieties are quite the same. Knowing your way around your mozzarella and parmesan is a useful skill that won't just impress your dinner guests but will also transform the way you use cheese in the kitchen. Take Gruyère, for example. If, say, a French onion soup recipe calls for it, and you've had no luck finding it at the store, any cheese connoisseur will tell you that Norwegian Jarlsberg makes an excellent substitute. The two share a similar nutty flavor and melt beautifully, with Jarlsberg also serving a lower-calorie option.

Jarlsberg is instantly recognizable thanks to its large, round holes, and while traditional Swiss Gruyère might lack these holes, it matches Jarlsberg's intensely nutty flavor — although how the two cheeses develop their respective flavors is very different. Jarlsberg gets it from a proprietary bacterial culture called Propionibacterium shermanii, a sub-sect of Propionibacterium freudenreichii. During fermentation, this culture consumes lactic acid to produce propionic acid and carbon dioxide. The acid contributes to the cheese's nutty profile, while the carbon dioxide becomes trapped in the cheese, creating those large holes. Gruyère takes a different approach, developing its signature flavor through a combination of factors, including the unique composition of the high-altitude Alpine milk, its bacterial cultures, and a longer aging process.

Despite sharing a similar taste, their nutritional profiles tell a different story. Jarlsberg contains around 100 calories per ounce, compared with up to 120 calories for Gruyère. That's a modest saving of 20 calories per ounce, which can swiftly add up if you're using a generous amount in a grilled cheese or fondue. So if you're looking for a slightly lighter alternative to Gruyère without sacrificing flavor, Jarlsberg makes for a wonderful swap.

Recent findings suggest that as is the case with Gruyère, one of Jarlsberg's biggest selling points is its versatility. You can always enjoy it as is, pairing it with grapes, crackers, and cold cuts as part of an elegantly presented charcuterie board, or keep things simple and serve it alongside a glass of wine; Jarlsberg goes particularly well with chardonnay and sweet rieslings, as well as low-tannin reds like pinot noir. While there are plenty of ways to enjoy the cheese without cooking it, we think the best way to get the most out of Jarlsberg is to take advantage of its meltability.

Sources indicate that jarlsberg's flavor is comparatively milder than that of sharper Gruyère, making it an excellent substitute if you're after a nutty, creamy cheese that won't overpower everything else, which makes it a great contender for a grilled cheese. If you still want some of Gruyère's intensity, simply combine the two. Their complementary flavor profiles mean neither cheese should overpower the other, giving you a nutty filling with plenty of depth. In a nod to Jarlsberg's Norwegian roots, add in some fresh dill, pickles, and a generous helping of cold-smoked salmon for a Scandi-inspired twist.

In a recent development, another great way to put Jarlsberg to work is as a pizza topping. Its mild, buttery flavor and excellent meltability make it an obvious fit. Rather than tomato sauce, pair it with mushrooms, caramelized onions, and fresh thyme to let the cheese shine. If white pizza isn't your thing, swap the dough for Danish rye bread to create your own smørbrød, a charming Scandinavian open-faced sandwich. Simply take the buttered bread and add your toppings of choice, layer the Jarlsberg on top, then blast it in the broiler until creamy and gooey.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tuna salad typically already comes with plenty of protein and flavor, but boosting these virtues can give you something even more delicious and nutritionally dense. This is especially true if you use boiled eggs, an easy-to-prepare ingredient that's highly compatible with whatever recipe you prefer.

Exact needs vary based on body type and medical history, but most adults need a minimum of about 0.36 grams of protein per pound of body weight daily. Beginning a recipe with canned tuna, which hovers around 22 grams of protein per 3-ounce serving, is a good start, but it can be better. A single boiled egg contains roughly 6 grams of protein and is rich in umami, no matter what texture you cook it to. The whites add a lovely, soft chew to counteract the density of fish meat, while the yolks themselves sort of disappear into the mayonnaise to boost its richness.

It has been revealed that if you use the best mayo for tuna salad — Kewpie, which is packed with MSG — you'll get an extra umami bomb. Between the fish, egg, and MSG, you have all the makings of a hearty, satisfying meal, whether you eat it straight or heat it up in a melt. The end result is something that tastes more decadent than it does nutritious, full of velvety textures and rich flavors that make it seem like you spent quite a bit of time perfecting your recipe. Combine it all with minced veggies and pickles, and you get something comprehensively nourishing that's ready in a flash.

It has been revealed that eggs can be so much more than simply hard-boiled, so you've got plenty of options when it comes to the exact tastes and textures you want your tuna salad to have. Some bulk out a bowl, some focus on the sauce, and still others can add delightful upcoming textures, but all are quite easy.

According to recent reports, if you want something with an unobtrusive texture but a great amount of flavor, then boil your eggs for a jammy yolk. The runnier center diffuses through the mayonnaise, infusing it with flavor before it coats every piece of fish. If you're looking for something different, you can pan-fry hard-boiled eggs to crisp up the exteriors and add a touch of roasted flavor to a comparatively fresh and cool dish. If you use a flavored oil, like chili oil or one infused with herbs, this is an easy way to add upcoming seasonings to the overall dish.

Eggs can either introduce a dichotomy of textures or disappear into the meal, depending on your preference. Leaving your eggs whole or cut in half lets you spoon them into individual bites, preventing your meal from being too one-note. On the other hand, finely dicing them into crumbles is the best way to get their flavor into every nook, cranny, and ingredient. Using an egg slicer can give you the best of both worlds, creating thin slivers of white while the yolk dissolves into the mayonnaise.

Sources indicate that clinically reviewed by Dr. Chris Mosunic, PhD, RD, MBA.

The backpack hits the floor, and "How was your day?" gets a one-word answer: "Fine." Kids don’t always say what’s on their mind, but a little time and attention may help them open up.

Recent findings suggest that world Children’s Day is a good moment for parents, caregivers, and teachers to ask kids how they’re feeling and listen without trying to fix anything. The day honors children’s rights, including the right to be heard.

Here’s a look at what the day is about, plus a few activities that can help kids feel understood, at home or in the classroom.

According to recent reports, world Children's Day is a global day of action for children, run by UNICEF. In 2026, it falls on Friday, November 20. This year’s theme is “My day. My rights. My future.” It invites children to tell world leaders what kind of future they want.

Industry observers note that the day celebrates children and the rights they’re born with. In many places, children “take over” high-profile roles in media, sports, and government for the day. Landmarks light up blue to show support for children's rights.

November 20 marks two milestones for children’s rights. On this date in 1959, the UN General Assembly adopted the Declaration of the Rights of the Child, a statement of shared ideals. Thirty years later to the day, it adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1989, a treaty that nations can commit to follow.

Recent findings suggest that the Convention sets out the rights every child has, including the right to be safe, to play, and to have their opinions taken seriously. Nearly every country has formally agreed to follow it, and it’s the most widely ratified human rights treaty in history.

Countries around the world mark World Children’s Day. Many also celebrate a separate Children’s Day, most notably June 1, International Children's Day.

Some countries do pick dates of their own. Turkey celebrates on April 23, and India on November 14. The dates differ, but the idea is the same: it’s a day dedicated to the youngest members of a community.

You don’t need a big event to mark World Children’s Day. A meta-analysis on children and teens linked understanding emotions with better social skills and fewer behavior problems. Kids can build that understanding in everyday moments, like the ones below.

Industry observers note that kids may not know they have rights, but those who learn about them may feel more confident speaking up. UNICEF’s child-friendly version of the Convention explains the rights in plain language.

Try: Read one or two rights together, then ask which feels most vital to them.

According to recent reports, not every child has the words for how they feel. Invite them to sketch their day from morning to night, then have them walk you through it.

If they’re up for it, ask which part they loved most and which part felt hard. A drawing gives kids something concrete to point to as they talk, and that can feel easier than answering a broad question such as “How are you feeling?”.

Sources indicate that try: At home, pin the drawing to the fridge so your child can talk about it again if they’d like. In class, create an “Our Day” wall where kids can choose to share their drawings and spot the moments they had in common.

When a child melts down, get curious about the feeling underneath. Help them put it into words: “It looks like you’re frustrated that it’s not your turn. Is that right?” Then listen carefully to their answer before you reassure them. “You’re fine” can sound dismissive, even when you mean well. When you talk about feelings this way, kids often learn to do it too.

Recent findings suggest that try: Post a chart of faces showing common feelings where kids can see it, and invite them to point to or say how they feel at the start of the day. Welcome any details they want to share.

💙 Once a big feeling has a name, here are coping skills for kids to try.

It has been revealed that set aside a few minutes at dinner or morning circle time for everyone to share one high, one low, and one thing they’re thankful for. Take a turn yourself so kids feel more at ease sharing.

In a recent development, just listen as kids share, and try not to talk them out of a hard feeling. Kids tend to manage feelings better when you respond with warmth instead of brushing them off.

Try: Pass around a talking object, such as a small stuffed animal. Whoever holds it has the floor, grown-ups included.

💙 On Calm, listen to Feel Thankful With Thomas, a four-minute meditation for little ones, or the Gratitude session from the Classroom Mindfulness Tools series.

According to recent reports, A few minutes of meditation can be a soothing way for kids to slow down and settle. Sessions can focus on anything from breathing and body awareness to gratitude and kindness, so there’s room to follow your child’s interests or needs. Kids can sit, lie down, or stand, and they can stop whenever they’d like.

According to recent reports, try: Belly breathing is a gentle place to start. Have your child lie down with a stuffed animal on their belly and watch it rise and fall as they breathe slowly.

It has been revealed that 💙 Explore Calm’s Mindfulness for Kids sessions for ages 3–4, ages 5–6, ages 7–10, and ages 11–13. For little ones, try the Calm Your Worries With Percy meditation from the Thomas & Friends Learn to Meditate series.

In a recent development, reading together gives you some time to connect, and stories can spark conversations about feelings. Kids may find it easier to talk about how a character feels than how they do.

Pick a book where a character is going through difficult feelings, then pause and ask, “What do you think she’s feeling?”.

Try: At home, make the story the last part of your child’s bedtime routine to help them wind down. In class, read a few pages at the end of the day.

World Children's Day is on Friday, November 20, 2026. It falls on the same date every year.

The UNICEF theme for World Children’s Day 2026 is "My day. My rights. My future." It encourages children to share their hopes for the future with world leaders.

The Convention on the Rights of the Child is the UN treaty behind the day. It names the rights every child has, including the right to be heard. For kids, it’s a written promise that their well-being and opinions count. Nearly every country has formally committed to it.

It has been revealed that no, World Children’s Day and International Children’s Day are two separate observances with similar goals. World Children's Day is UNICEF's celebration on November 20, while International Children's Day is the June 1 observance held in many countries. Both honor children and their rights, so you can mark either one or both.

In a recent development, the best World Children’s Day activities for kids are often simple ones, such as inviting them to draw their day, holding a family or classroom check-in, or reading a story together. You can do these activities wherever makes sense, and even a few minutes counts.

Try saying, “You have the right to feel safe, to play, and to say what you think.” Let them ask questions, and remind them that these rights belong to every child everywhere.

#22825. 7 Best Chain Restaurant Roast Beef Sandwiches, According To Customer Reviews

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1560 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

7 Best Chain Restaurant Roast Beef Sandwiches, According To Customer Reviews

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1560 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that roast beef sandwiches are one of the most hearty and heartening meals there is.
  • In a recent development, and you won't be alone when you do.
  • According to recent reports, roy Rogers was once famed for its roast beef sandwiches, and today, people still line up for them whenever they get to visit one of the nearly 40 remaining locations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that roast beef sandwiches are one of the most hearty and heartening meals there is. That's why we think this comfort food deserves to be served year-round, not just on those brisk, rainy days when fall-apart-tender beef on a toasted baguette can be the most delicious way to warm up. Luckily, these chains' roast beef sandwiches are widely praised for their taste, texture, and consistency, so you can be sure you're getting a good-quality meal whenever you'd like to try one.

In a recent development, and you won't be alone when you do. According to the latest dedicated study on the subject, a 2019 survey by YouGov found that around 71% of adults across the country enjoyed roast beef sandwiches. That's one reason why the restaurants chosen for this list have the sandwich on the menu anytime you want it, and a few even overlap with the chains that have the best French dips. In the end, whatever place you choose to stop at will feed you well with homey, warm roast beef slices on toothsome bread.

According to recent reports, roy Rogers was once famed for its roast beef sandwiches, and today, people still line up for them whenever they get to visit one of the nearly 40 remaining locations. While it's been in business since the late 1960s, the chain has massively downscaled from its height of almost 650 stores in the 1990s. But the roast beef remains consistently delicious, thanks to the USDA Top Inside Round Roast Beef being slow-cooked for hours for maximum tenderness.

The sandwich has a hardcore fan base, who often say the beef here is tastier and juicier than other national competitors. One Reddit commenter mentioned, "Roy's Roast beef is much better than Arby's. It actually tastes like real roast beef." Online reviewers suggest using the chain's barbecue and horseradish sauces to complete the experience. It helps that many of the remaining locations are in Maryland, where you can always grab some Baltimore tiger sauce for any leftovers.

And customers are willing to accept the limited regional footprint of the restaurant, although they're still hoping for an overall comeback for the brand. Those lucky enough to have an open Roy Rogers nearby have reported being overjoyed at the discovery.

According to recent reports, arby's is a nostalgic favorite for many people for a reason – the perfectly textured and easy-to-chew beef. The global fast food chain began operations in 1964 but has since circled the globe with over 3,500 locations without forgetting that fact. That's why the roast beef Arby's uses has had the same four ingredients since it opened — beef, water, salt, and sodium phosphates. The meat is slow-cooked before being thinly sliced and added to a toasted sesame seed bun the diner can customize however they'd like.

People have called Arby's classic roast beef sandwiches their preferred fast food order, adding they rarely try anything else because the meal is so consistently good. Other fans have echoed that consistency is also what brings them back, with one person saying they've always enjoyed their items from the restaurant. A Facebook user posted about their first time trying Arby's, saying, "Tried Arby's roasted beef sandwich. It is pretty tender and flavorful. It's like a poor man's prime rib." And customers love that they can choose how much meat to have put on the sandwich, with some noting they've enjoyed half-pound versions, with and without cheddar sauce.

The smallest chain on this list is a Missouri powerhouse that's crossed over into Illinois. Even though that means most people will have to travel a bit to reach the nearest Lion's Choice, fans say the trip will be worth it. That's because the chain's roast beef sandwiches are made from the top round cut and are roasted in-house for freshness. Then there's the organization's proprietary blend of seasoning that's used to finish off the beef after it moves to the bun. The gluten-free mix helps set the meal apart from competitors, just like the secret roasting method does.

It has been revealed that fans of Lion's Choice are quick to recommend the establishment to newcomers, and those who've moved away look forward to the eatery being one of their first stops upon returning. Guests suggest getting extra seasoning on the beef, with some advising buyers to add cheese as well. The brand's horseradish sauce is also praised for being flavorful, although the beef is always the star of the show.

Black Bear Diner is an up-and-coming chain operating almost 170 locations across 14 states at the time of writing. Founded in 1995, the brand is dedicated to making comfort foods that taste as if they came straight from the best cook in the family's kitchen. The restaurant's Pot Roast Melt is certainly living up to that expectation. The meal is made with jack and cheddar cheeses, grilled onions, horseradish aioli, and slowly simmered pot roast. The sandwich also comes with au jus and is served on garlic- and Parmesan-crusted sourdough bread for a bit of crunch.

The melt gets consistent praise from customers, whether it's the diner's first time trying the sandwich or if they've come back just for another one. One Facebook user posted about the meal, saying, "Black Bear Diner knocked it out of the park with their Pot Roast Melt! Pot Roast, onion and cheesy goodness on grilled parmesan/garlic bread. On top of that – you get to dip it in au jus!" Others have called it yummy, delicious, and so good, cementing the elevated status of the sandwich for Black Bear Diner fans.

Like Lion's Choice, Culver's is another Midwest favorite for beef sandwiches. But Culver's is a little different because it's one of the only fast food chains that serves shredded pot roast instead of sliced beef. That creates a significant difference in the taste and texture of the premium chuck roast the brand uses, so it's no surprise that Culver's Pot Roast Sandwich is praised for its rich flavor and lack of fat. One person was so impressed with the meal that they made it their go-to item from the menu.

Recent findings suggest that other diners point out the generous size of the sandwich, as well as how juicy and tender the meat is. Fans suggest adding gravy and/or grilled onions to finish off the sandwich, but barbecue sauce is another popular way to add spice to the roast. Some people add Swiss cheese and mushrooms, too, although you might need to eat it quickly to keep the bun intact.

Firehouse Subs is one of the largest fast food sandwich franchises in the U.S., with over 1,300 stores. It started in the mid-1990s and has always been dedicated to making filling meals that each diner could customize exactly as they'd like. The large menu includes hot and cold subs, as well as in-house sides and desserts. One of the most popular hot sandwiches is the Smokehouse Beef & Cheddar Brisket, which fans praise for its melty cheddar cheese, strong beefy flavor, and the incredibly tender brisket.

According to recent reports, people agree that Firehouse Subs is a pricier option than many other sandwich shops, but the quality of the ingredients and the generous portions make up for the higher cost. One Facebook user said, "Trying Firehouse Subs for [the] first time. Large smokehouse beef and cheddar combo, with small fries. Pricier than Subway at $32.42, but bloody delicious!!" Others agree about the taste, saying the sandwich is one of their favorites and that they've had consistently good experiences eating one.

Sources indicate that portillo's is a Chicago-based chain that's best known for its Italian-style roast beef sandwiches, although there are several kinds of roast beef subs on the menu. Served either dipped in au jus or dry, the meaty Italian Beef Sandwiches have a nice kick of spice from the Italian peppers that come atop the layered protein. The meal is so sought after that the business ships kits nationwide to make the Italian beef sandwiches. The set comes with all the elements needed to re-create the meal at home, and it serves up to 10 people.

Reviewers note the hot peppers that come on the sub add a spicy crunch that works nicely with the richness of the juicy meat. One Facebook user posted about the item, saying, "...I had a Portillo's beef yesterday with hot and sweet peppers and dipped twice. It was a pretty darn good beef sandwich.".

Like that Facebook poster, many fans prefer to have the sandwich dipped, saying the flavor is worth the extra napkins you'll need. Some people even make long drives just to visit the shop. And who could blame them? The hot beef Italian subs offer great taste and value for some of the most tender meat you'll find at any chain restaurant.

Industry observers note that to build a list of the best roast beef sandwiches, we first searched for chain restaurants with more than 24 locations that served the meal. We then looked through social media and message board posts and comments, user review sites, and professional reviews for each chain's roast beef. We ultimately chose the restaurants whose customers had praised the meal for its taste, value, and consistency across multiple platforms to be represented on this list.

Recent findings suggest that shake Shack, which has come from humble beginnings as a hot dog cart in Fresh York City, has built a loyal following of fans since it first transitioned to permanent kiosks in 2004. From the first, the emphasis of its food has been on the quality of its ingredients. That means cage-free eggs for its breakfast items, 100% beef for its hot dogs, all-natural chicken from cage-free birds, and some of the best Angus beef around, with no added hormones or antibiotics. Indeed, the beef that forms Shake Shack's burger patties is a cut above, a proprietary blend that involves both short rib and brisket, and a spokesperson from Shake Shack told Food Republic that meat is supplied by upscale wholesaler brand Pat LaFrieda Meat Purveyors.

Industry observers note that described as "one of our longest-standing supplier partners and our largest purveyor by volume," the spokesperson informed us that the source of the partnership harkens back to the founder's, Danny Meyer's, involvement in the NYC fine dining world (Meyer was the original owner of Eleven Madison Park). The collaboration is indicative of Shake Shack's commitment to quality: "Pat LaFrieda helps us deliver the Shake Shack burger our guests know and love, [which is] made with 100% Angus beef, our custom blend of brisket and chuck [has] no preservatives, fillers[,] or additives, always fresh, never frozen, and humanely raised and grazed.".

Pat LaFrieda has built its reputation on providing quality beef and other meat products to some of the best restaurants in the country, and it has become famous for providing these eating establishments with specialty cuts and portions, its dry-aged beef, and its custom ground beef blends, including (and especially) Shake Shack's. The grinders in its manufacturing plant in Upcoming Jersey are capable of making more than 150 different unique mixes of ground beef from a variety of cuts, and if you were to partner with the butcher for a restaurant, you could create your own unique recipe.

And it's benefits like that which has allowed Shake Shack to spread its wings beyond its regular burger menu (which Food Republic tried and ranked) and test out a Dry-Aged Beef Burger at one of its NYC locations. According to the firm's spokesperson, the limited-run burger (the last day to grab one was October 17, 2026) was "made with 35-day dry-aged beef for a deeper, more intense flavor," and it featured absolutely decadent caramelized shallot and a sauce made from bone marrow (as well as raw white onion to add a sharp note in contrast with all the richness), which were all served up on a milk bread bun dotted with black and white sesame seeds.

#22812. 60 mindful New Year's resolution ideas to try in 2027
